# Platform differences

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_shared_contracts.py --write-report from
     scripts/ci/platform-differences.toml and scripts/ci/clone-baseline.toml. Do not edit by
     hand; the default check fails when this file is stale. -->

Every difference between products (Piers, Decks) must be **earned**: an
operating-system API or behaviour forces it. Anything else is a gap to
close or logic to move to `shared/`. This page is the ledger of both.

- **Earned differences** name the OS API or behaviour and cite the code.
- **Open gaps** are differences nobody has earned. Each has an owner; it
  closes when parity lands or when it is earned with evidence. "Not
  implemented yet" and "not possible" are different statements.
- `python3 scripts/check_shared_contracts.py` fails when an OS-conditional
  `cfg` in `shared/` has no row, a citation no longer holds, the
  capability matrix disagrees with the code, a new local copy of shared
  logic appears, a `platform` config key has no row, or cross-product
  clones grow past the baseline.

To add a difference, edit the ledger and run
`python3 scripts/check_shared_contracts.py --write-report`.

| PD-018 | file security | Windows Pier, macOS Deck, Windows Deck, `shared/deck-core`, `shared/observability` | Private-file checks and creation modes. | POSIX mode bits, owner and O_NOFOLLOW on Unix; security descriptors, owners and reparse points on Windows, where files inherit an ACL instead of taking a mode. A file without a name while open (a sealed support bundle's plaintext) is unlink-while-open on Unix and FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE on Windows, which cannot unlink an open file; FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT opens a reparse point instead of following it. A support-bundle source path is walked folder by folder: on Unix with openat(O_NOFOLLOW) relative to the folder before (rustix), following only a link whose owner and folder (uid, mode bits) show nobody else could have made it, and opening the file O_NONBLOCK so a FIFO cannot block; Win32 has no open relative to a handle and no owner/mode facts for a reparse point, so every folder is opened by path with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, any reparse point is refused, and each handle's GetFinalPathNameByHandleW location must sit inside the one before. Identity is fstat device and inode on Unix; on Windows the 64-bit volume serial and 128-bit FILE_ID_128 from GetFileInformationByHandleEx(FileIdInfo) (the 64-bit index only where FileIdInfo is unsupported), with GetVolumeInformationByHandleW's FILE_SUPPORTS_OPEN_BY_FILE_ID and FileRemoteProtocolInfo saying whether the volume can prove it (std exposes none of these on stable). Desk privacy's default proves the hook thread with the keyboard canary (InputHookGuard::install_keyboard_proved); blocking a physical desk mouse is unit-tested, not lab-proven (the lab Pier has no desk mouse). The mouse hook is given only the low 32 bits of an event's dwExtraInfo, so Arcen's injection markers are 32-bit: through 0.20.8 a 64-bit marker made the hook swallow every move, button and wheel a Deck sent (no pointer, no clicks), which an earlier note here misread as Windows never calling WH_MOUSE_LL for an injected move. | Windows Host | `hosts/windows/src/deskside.rs` (`InputHookGuard`)<br>`hosts/windows/src/input.rs` (`InjectSyntheticPointerInput`) |
| GAP-042 | session model | Linux Pier | The Linux Pier joins the account's own GNOME Wayland console session (shared `console_session::wayland_join` and `wayland_attach`, Linux `session/wayland/join.rs`): its compositor proven, its own monitors recorded as they run, input and clipboard through its own RemoteDesktop session, served only when capture, input and lock are proved, locked when the Deck leaves. Unlike an X11 console it is not held for a resume (GNOME closes sharing on lock), a session shown on a monitor at the desk is served with its screens reported visible, or refused when desk privacy is required (`desk_privacy`: a Wayland desk cannot be blanked without changing the compositor), and a Wayland login screen is still refused `console_wayland_session` (ADR 0025 section 9). | The join has shipped: S4a (the target and ownership contract), S4c-2 (no desktop beside an account's session) and S4b (the join, its desk-privacy judgement, the lock on leaving or on a monitor change at the desk, and the join journal), proved on a task-owned GNOME 49 session without a display connector. Still missing: keeping a physical desk monitor private without changing the compositor; a remote-first sign-in through a Wayland login screen (GDM 47 has no third-party route; GDM 50 adds CreateUserDisplay, not used yet); the resume hold across a lock; persistent per-user Wayland sessions on a host without Xorg (`wayland-persistent-session`); laying the session's own monitors out to a Deck that matches its layout (Mutter's `org.gnome.Mutter.DisplayConfig.ApplyMonitorsConfig`, not used yet; ADR 0025 section 6); and native proof on a host with a display connector and GDM's login screen. | Linux Host | `shared/session/src/console_session/wayland_attach.rs` (`desk_privacy`)<br>`shared/session/src/console_session/wayland_attach.rs` (`AFTER_DECK_LEFT`)<br>`hosts/linux/src/session/wayland/join.rs` (`JoinedSession`) |
| GAP-043 | session model | macOS Pier | The Linux and Windows Piers name, in the refusal a Deck shows, the other remote-desktop service that holds the workstation, as the host reports it at run time (`console_session::ForeignService`, `ConsoleNotice`: Linux the PAM service and the system service that started the session, Windows the session's WinStation listener and client protocol); the macOS Pier names the console owner only. | Not implemented yet: macOS has no other-product console session model yet. It would build the same shared ConsoleNotice. | Shared/Architecture | `shared/session/src/console_session/foreign_service.rs` (`ConsoleNotice`) |
| GAP-055 | observability | macOS Pier | The Linux and Windows Piers write a service-wide HEALTH_SNAPSHOT each minute, the worst state any session committed (shared `ServiceHealth`; the Windows broker hears it from its session agents); the macOS Pier writes only each stream's own snapshot, from its own frame-rate verdict. | Not implemented yet: the macOS stream runs the shared SessionHealth (HealthStatsReporter), but its committed state is not passed out of HealthStatsReporter::report, and the network service has no ServiceHealth and no agent relay message to hear it, as the Windows broker does. | macOS Host | `hosts/macos/src/stream.rs` (`emit_health_snapshot`) |
| GAP-057 | session lifecycle | Windows Pier | When the operating system signs the session out or shuts down under a live Deck, the Windows Pier writes the session's end (`signed_out`, `host_shutdown`) and its service stop (`host_shutdown`) within the shared `host_shutdown` budget: the agent from a hidden window's WM_ENDSESSION, the service from PRESHUTDOWN with a bounded drain. The Linux and macOS Piers have not adopted the shared contract. | Not audited yet on Linux and macOS: whether a Pier there records a session the operating system ends under a live Deck (systemd's stop of the Pier and logind's end of the user session at shutdown; launchd and loginwindow on macOS) is unproven. Each would use the same `StopCause`, `DrainDeadline` and `SessionTally`. | Shared/Architecture | `shared/session/src/host_shutdown.rs` (`SessionTally`)<br>`hosts/windows/src/session_end.rs` (`WM_ENDSESSION`)<br>`hosts/windows/src/service.rs` (`SERVICE_CONTROL_PRESHUTDOWN`) |
| GAP-058 | media | Linux Pier | In a ten-bit 4:4:4 contract (Grading, HDR) the Windows Pier refuses a display's own 4:2:0 request through the shared `arcen_media::region_chroma`, serves it 4:4:4 and publishes `chroma_420_outside_full_color_contract` on that display's applied media plan; the Linux Pier's multi-monitor planner still serves such a display ten-bit 4:2:0 and publishes no per-display reason. | Not implemented yet: the Linux planner keeps its own per-intent chroma match and its applied-region assembler carries only a session-wide reason. It would call the shared rule and publish the refusal per display; proof needs a Linux lab that serves Grading on two displays. | Linux Host | `shared/media/src/multi_monitor.rs` (`region_chroma`)<br>`hosts/linux/src/media/multi_capenc.rs` (`BandwidthOptimized`) |
| GAP-059 | media | Linux Pier | The Windows Pier publishes, on the applied media plan of each Match My Layout display that encoder admission serves on OpenH264 beside NVENC displays, the shared `EncoderSetDecision::region_encoder_degradations` reason (`hardware_encoder_ceiling`, `encoder_reassigned_by_capacity`, `encoder_reassigned_after_probe_failure`) as a degradation; the Linux Pier admits mixed sets through the same shared admission but publishes no per-display reason. | Not implemented yet: the Linux applied-region assembler carries one session-wide reason. It would publish the shared per-display reasons as the Windows Pier does. | Linux Host | `shared/media/src/encoder_admission.rs` (`region_encoder_degradations`) |
| GAP-060 | displays | Linux Pier | The Windows and macOS Piers, and the Linux Pier on an Xorg console, read their displays before and after a Deck and print them with `arcen-pier diagnose displays`; on a GNOME Wayland console (Mutter virtual monitors) the Linux Pier reads neither, so that restore is not proved and the command reports that a Wayland console is not read yet. | Not implemented yet: Mutter's `org.gnome.Mutter.DisplayConfig.GetCurrentState` reports each monitor's mode, refresh, scale, transform, primary and colour mode; a reader would fill the same shared `DisplayTruth`. | Linux Host | `hosts/linux/src/session/diagnose.rs` (`pub fn diagnose_main`) |

## Capability matrix

Checked against production code: "yes" must be provable by the
capability's proof pattern, and a PD or GAP cell must not be.

### Piers

| Capability | Linux Pier | Windows Pier | macOS Pier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sends host_keymap | yes | yes | yes |
| Throttles failed sign-ins | yes | yes | yes |
| Limits pre-sign-in connections per source address | yes | yes | yes |
| Refuses an unservable video request after the password, with its reason, not as a failed sign-in | yes | yes | yes |
| Loads TLS material through arcen_transport::host_material | yes | yes | yes |
| Reloads TLS material while serving, keeping the last good material on a refused replacement, and emits the shared certificate lifecycle events (active, expiring, reloaded, reload failed, expired) | yes | yes | yes |
| Writes the service's minute HEALTH_SNAPSHOT from its sessions' committed health | yes | yes | GAP-055 |
| Direct session resume | yes | yes | GAP-003 |
| Native (USB-bridged) tablet | yes | yes | yes |
| Mutes local playback while streaming | yes | yes | yes |
| Keeps the machine awake while serving | yes | yes | yes |
| Deskside privacy | yes | yes | yes |
| Grayscale font smoothing while streaming | GAP-015 | yes | PD-012 |
| The Pier gives a desktop it starts the account's locale | yes | PD-042 | PD-042 |
| Time zone restored through a durable lease | yes | yes | GAP-017 |
| Disconnected-session idle timeout | yes | PD-004 | PD-004 |
| Carries host audio captured at any device rate from 8 to 384 kHz as audio-v1 through the shared resampler (GAP-055 closed) | PD-016 | yes | yes |
| Moves windows a session stranded back to a visible display | yes | yes | PD-032 |
| Support bundles pseudonymise host names and addresses by one shared rule | yes | yes | yes |
| Crash reports enter a support bundle only when asked, and the manifest records the choice | yes | yes | yes |
| A support bundle can include the product's own crash reports | GAP-040 | GAP-040 | GAP-040 |
| The hello says which PC keys beyond F12 and the main block the Pier injects (pc_keys), from the shared PC-key table | yes | yes | yes |
| Locks the user's session when a Deck leaves, then gives the desk its monitors and input back | yes | yes | yes |
| Locks the user's session before the desk gets it back when the Pier process serving a Deck dies while attached | yes | yes | yes |
| A refusal because another remote-desktop service holds the workstation names that service as the host reports it | yes | yes | GAP-043 |
| Clicks the desktop's right button for pen button bit 0 and its middle button for bit 1, and says so (pen_button_actions) | yes | yes | yes |

identical normalised lines (comments, tests and lines of only
punctuation removed), on the larger side of each pair. A pair may
shrink, never grow.
